title: PROMPTING GPT-3 TO BE RELIABLE
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured social biases against people from nine protected classes, including religion. Specifically, it assessed whether the model would select a stereotypical (pro-bias) answer, a counter-stereotypical (anti-bias) answer, or a neutral answer in ambiguous and unambiguous contexts related to religion.
findings: Using a balanced prompt with examples from different demographic distributions helps reduce religious bias in GPT-3. Conversely, using biased prompts (e.g., only pro-stereotype examples) significantly increases the model's bias scores. A key finding is that adding a natural language instruction to the prompt, such as 'We should treat people from different ... religions ... equally,' effectively guides the model to make more neutral predictions and significantly reduces bias scores.
references: Udit Arora, William Huang, and He He. Types of out-of-distribution texts and how to detect them. In EMNLP, 2021.
